item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q003_actin_like_atpase_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, these catalytic domains are separate families within the same Actin-like ATPase domain superfamily, c.55.1 (SUNID 53067): Actin/HSP70 is c.55.1.1 (SUNID 53068), hexokinase is c.55.1.3 (SUNID 53083), and glycerol kinase is c.55.1.4 (SUNID 53089). The superfamily lies in the Ribonuclease H-like motif fold c.55 and class c, Alpha and beta proteins (a/b). Thus SCOPe supports remote domain-level homology—a probable common ancestor and a conserved actin-like ATP-binding/catalytic structural core—rather than mere same-fold analogy. It does not justify transferring the proteins’ substrate specificity, precise reaction, cellular role, regulation, oligomeric state, or whole-protein architecture. Cross-family structural templates may guide modeling of the conserved core, but family-specific representatives are preferable for active-site details, insertions, conformational states, and domain organization.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/; /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop: /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Actin%2FHSP70&mode=auto&limit=1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=hexokinase&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=glycerol+kinase&mode=auto&limit=20","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51349; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53066; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53067; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53068; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53083; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53089"]}]}
